description: The Sun Yat-Sen University UGS-1m research team publishes Python components for UGSNet, a model for extracting urban green space from high-resolution imagery. The repository contains encoder, decoder, discriminator, attention, point-rendering and sampling modules. Its documented application maps 31 Chinese cities at approximately one-metre resolution, using a labelled UGSet benchmark and adaptation between cities. Zenodo archives the code with an other-open licence label and free public access; GitHub does not identify more specific software terms. That licensing uncertainty should be resolved before relying on a particular redistribution permission. The inspected README describes the architecture and links the data, but does not provide a complete tested training command or verified pretrained weights. The components can support inspection and adaptation of vegetation-mapping methods used to prepare heat or drainage simulation inputs. They complement the finished UGS maps with the published model architecture. No model was trained or run.
